github.description: OAuth login + App installation credentials for GitHub.
github.name: App name
github.nameHelp: GitHub App names are globally unique. Pick a suffix that's distinct — e.g. your GitHub handle or org slug.
github.privateKeyHelp: Paste the full contents of the .pem file generated by GitHub.
github.manifestHelp: Create a new GitHub App in one click. You'll be redirected to GitHub to confirm the manifest, then returned here with credentials pre-filled.
github.orPasteBelow: Or paste credentials for an existing app below.
github.publicUrlHelp: Publicly reachable URL where this backend is served — used by GitHub for OAuth callback and webhook delivery. In dev, paste your tunnel URL (e.g. ngrok).
github.orgSlugHelp: The URL fragment for your org (e.g. 'my-org' from github.com/my-org). You must be an owner.
github.homepageUrlHelp: Shown on the App's GitHub page. Defaults to the frontend URL in your backend config — override if the frontend lives on a different host.
github.callbackUrlHelp: Where GitHub redirects after user authorization. Leave blank to use {backend}/auth/callback/github.
github.webhookUrlHelp: Where GitHub delivers event payloads. Leave blank to use {backend}/webhooks/github.
github.setupUrlHelp: Where users land after installing the App. Leave blank to use {frontend}/admin.
github.deleteWarning: Deleting here only removes the credentials from this instance. GitHub does not expose an API to delete the App itself — you'll need to remove it manually from GitHub settings if you want to reuse the name.

gitlab.webhookSecretHelp: Shared secret used to verify incoming GitLab webhooks (X-Gitlab-Token header).

llm.heading: LLM credentials
llm.description: An ordered pool of credentials — tried in priority order, with automatic failover when one is rate limited.
llm.oauthTokenHelp: Generate with `claude setup-token` — runs Claude Code against your Anthropic subscription (no API key or model needed).
llm.planTierHelp: Informational only — not used to decide when a credential is exhausted.
llm.modelHighHelp: Used for reasoning-heavy work like drafting fixes.
llm.modelHeavyHelp: Optional. Triage can move the fixer to this model for clearly heavy work, or when the issue asks for it. Leave empty to never escalate.
llm.name: Name
llm.nameHelp: Optional. How issues refer to this credential to run the fixer on it, e.g. "self-hosted".
llm.modelLowHelp: Used for cheap utility calls like summaries and parsing.
llm.confirmRemove: Remove this credential from the pool? Dispatch will no longer be able to use it.

form.authTypeHelp: API key / JWT: one static token sent in a header on every request. Basic auth: a username/password pair, sent Base64-encoded. OAuth2: Jeanclode mints and refreshes an access token itself from a client_id/client_secret — nothing to rotate by hand. No auth: the host is only made reachable from the sandbox, with nothing injected — for public endpoints (a package registry, a CDN a skill downloads from).
form.skillAuthTypesNote: Skills support API key, JWT, Basic auth and No auth. Add one auth per host the skill calls.
form.editingNote: Editing an existing credential. The secret isn't shown back for editing — re-enter it below to save any change.
form.envVarNameHelp: The environment variable the skill's script reads this value as — check the skill's own instructions for the name it expects (e.g. OUTLINE_API_KEY).
form.tokenHelpApiKey: The API key value itself, exactly as issued by the provider — no header name or prefix, just the secret.
form.tokenHelpJwt: The JWT itself (the full token string). Jeanclode sends it as-is on every request — it does not renew or re-sign an expired token for you, so use a long-lived one if the provider offers it.
form.advanced: Advanced: header name and value prefix
form.headerHelp: The HTTP header the token is sent in. Defaults to Authorization — only change this if the skill's instructions say otherwise.
form.valuePrefixHelp: Text prepended to the token in the header, e.g. "Bearer ". Clear it if the API expects the raw token with no prefix.
form.usernameHelp: Sent Base64-encoded as the Authorization: Basic header on every request — the provider's login/service-account name.
form.passwordHelp: Paired with the username above into the Basic auth header. Use an API password or app-specific token if the provider offers one, rather than a personal login password.
form.clientIdHelp: From the provider's OAuth2 app/service-account settings — identifies which application is requesting a token.
form.clientSecretHelp: Paired with the Client ID to authenticate the token request. Treated the same as any other secret — never shown back once saved.
form.tokenUrlHelp: The provider's OAuth2 token endpoint Jeanclode calls to mint an access token — usually ends in /oauth/token or /token. Not the API's base URL.
form.grantTypeHelp: How Jeanclode mints the access token itself, headlessly, with no browser step — client_credentials from just the client ID/secret, password from a username/password pair, or refresh_token from a long-lived refresh token. Not offered: authorization_code, which needs an interactive redirect Jeanclode has no way to complete on its own.
form.scopeHelp: Space-separated OAuth2 scopes to request, if the provider requires specific ones. Leave blank to request the client's default scope.
form.oauthUsernameHelp: The resource owner's username for the password grant — sent to the token endpoint alongside the client ID/secret to mint an access token.
form.oauthPasswordHelp: Paired with the username above. Use an API password or app-specific credential if the provider offers one, rather than a personal login password.
form.refreshTokenHelp: A refresh token already issued by the provider (outside Jeanclode). Exchanged for a fresh access token on every mint — if the provider rotates refresh tokens on use, this won't keep working past the first exchange, since there's no interactive flow here to capture the new one.
form.hostHelp: All outbound traffic from the agent goes through a security proxy that only forwards requests to hosts it knows about. A skill has no declared host of its own (unlike an MCP server), so this tells the proxy which host to allow through and to inject this credential into — e.g. wiki.example.com for a wiki API key. It should match the host the skill's own instructions call out to. If an API is split across subdomains (e.g. api.example.com, www.example.com), use a wildcard like *.example.com to cover all of them — it matches any subdomain but not the bare example.com itself.
form.noneNote: Nothing is injected: requests to this host are just allowed out of the sandbox.
form.envVarNameBasicHelp: Only if the skill checks that a variable is set before calling the host. It gets a placeholder value — the real header is added on the wire.
form.hostHelpMcp: Leave blank to authenticate the MCP server itself. Set another host to authenticate an API the server's tools call.

welcome.title: Welcome to Jeanclode
welcome.body: Jeanclode works on your code by itself. It fixes Sentry errors, reviews pull requests, and solves GitHub and GitLab issues. This guide shows you each page and explains every setting.

stats.title: Your numbers
stats.hint: A quick look at what Jeanclode is doing.
stats.body: Running now is how many tasks Jeanclode is working on at this moment. Successful runs and PRs reviewed show what it finished in the last 30 days.

topUsers.title: Most active teammate
topUsers.hint: Who asked Jeanclode for help the most.
topUsers.body: Every time someone writes `{'@'}jeanclode-bot` in a comment, it counts. This card shows who does it the most.

live.title: Tasks in progress
live.hint: What Jeanclode is working on right now.
live.body: Each card is one task: fixing an error, reviewing a PR, or solving an issue. Click a card to see the details. You can stop a task while it's running.

prList.title: All your pull requests
prList.hint: Pull requests from all your repos.
prList.body: You see every pull request from your connected repos here, whether Jeanclode or your team opened it. The Status column shows what Jeanclode last did on each one.

prReview.title: Get a review
prReview.hint: Click Review to get feedback on your PR.
prReview.body: Jeanclode reads the code and leaves comments on the PR, like a teammate would. Click Review on one of your PRs, or add the `jeanclode:review` label to any PR on GitHub or GitLab. The `jeanclode:summary` label writes the PR description for you.

prLoop.title: It fixes its own comments
prLoop.hint: Jeanclode keeps going until the PR is clean.
prLoop.body: On a PR that Jeanclode opened, it doesn't stop at comments. It fixes what it found, pushes the change, and reviews again. When nothing is left to fix, it tells your team the PR is ready.

prFilters.title: Find a PR
prFilters.hint: Filter by status, date or repo.
prFilters.body: By default you see open PRs from the last 7 days. Change the filters to find older, merged or closed PRs.

issueSources.title: All your issues
issueSources.hint: Errors and issues, grouped by where they come from.
issueSources.body: This page lists Sentry errors and GitHub or GitLab issues together. Use the tabs to see one source at a time.

issueList.title: Where each issue stands
issueList.hint: The status shows what happened to each issue.
issueList.body: Pending means nothing has started yet. After that, the status shows whether Jeanclode is working on it, finished, or failed. Click an issue to see what Jeanclode did.

issueFix.title: Fix an issue now
issueFix.hint: Click Fix or Resolve to start right away.
issueFix.body: Fix is for a Sentry error. Resolve is for a GitHub or GitLab issue. You can also start it from GitHub or GitLab: add the `jeanclode:resolve` label, or comment "{'@'}jeanclode-bot take care of this".

issueMapped.title: Only issues Jeanclode can fix
issueMapped.hint: Hide errors that aren't linked to a repo yet.
issueMapped.body: Jeanclode can only fix a Sentry error once it knows which repo holds the code. Turn this on to hide the errors that aren't linked yet. You link them in the Sentry settings.

gitRepos.title: Choose your repos
gitRepos.hint: Jeanclode only works on repos that are turned on.
gitRepos.body: Find this in Integrations, on your GitHub or GitLab page. When a repo is off, Jeanclode ignores it completely: no reviews, no fixes, no replies.

gitRelated.title: Link repos that work together
gitRelated.hint: Let a fix in one repo also change the other.
gitRelated.body: Some bugs span two repos, like a website and its API. Link them, and a fix in one repo can also read and change the other.

gitAlwaysInclude.title: Repos every fix can see
gitAlwaysInclude.hint: Added to every fix, whatever the repo.
gitAlwaysInclude.body: Useful for a shared library, or when bugs are reported in one repo but the code lives in another. Jeanclode opens these repos every time it fixes an issue or a Sentry error.

gitTrigger.title: Who can call Jeanclode
gitTrigger.body: Developers only: only people who can push to the repo can call the bot. Anyone: everyone who can comment can call it, including people outside your team on public repos.

gitNotify.title: Who hears when a PR is ready
gitNotify.hint: These people get tagged when a PR is ready.
gitNotify.body: When Jeanclode finishes a PR it opened, it tags these people in a comment so they can check it and merge it. It never does this on PRs your team opened.

gitSubgroup.title: Nearby repos (GitLab)
gitSubgroup.hint: Let a fix see the other repos in the same folder.
gitSubgroup.body: In GitLab, repos are grouped in folders called subgroups. With this on, a fix can also look at the other repos in its subgroup. Very large subgroups are skipped because they would slow the fix down.

gitWebhooks.title: Project webhooks (GitLab Free)
gitWebhooks.body: Jeanclode normally listens to your whole GitLab group at once. GitLab Free can't do that, so turn this on and Jeanclode connects to each project one by one. This needs a token with Maintainer access.

gitTools.title: Extra tools
gitTools.hint: Give Jeanclode access to your other tools.
gitTools.body: Connect tools like your docs or your ticket tracker. Jeanclode can then look things up in them while it works, just like a teammate would.

sentryMapping.title: Link Sentry to your code
sentryMapping.hint: Tell Jeanclode which repo each Sentry project belongs to.
sentryMapping.body: Find this in Integrations, on your Sentry page. Each Sentry project needs a repo, or Jeanclode can't fix its errors. Click Auto-resolve to link them for you, then correct any that are wrong.

sentryAutofix.title: Fix errors automatically
sentryAutofix.hint: Automatic fixes new errors without waiting for you.
sentryAutofix.body: Manual only: errors wait on the Issues page until you click Fix. Automatic: Jeanclode fixes new errors on its own. The next settings only apply in Automatic mode.

sentryBatch.title: When and how many
sentryBatch.hint: How long to wait, and how many errors per fix.
sentryBatch.body: Jeanclode waits a little before it starts, so related errors end up in the same PR. Batch window is how long it waits. Batch size is the most errors it handles in one go.

sentryGate.title: Don't pile up PRs
sentryGate.hint: Wait until your team has handled the last PRs.
sentryGate.body: With this on, Jeanclode won't start new fixes until every PR from the last round is merged or closed. Your team never gets flooded with PRs.

sentryImport.title: Bring in older errors
sentryImport.hint: Also bring in errors that were already in Sentry.
sentryImport.body: New errors always come in. Choose how far back to also bring in older ones, so they show up on the Issues page. Click Import now to do it right away.

settingsAccounts.title: Your accounts
settingsAccounts.hint: Connect your GitHub and GitLab accounts.
settingsAccounts.body: Find this in Settings. Connecting your accounts tells Jeanclode which PRs and issues are yours, for example for the My PRs filter. You need at least one connected to sign in.

settingsMembers.title: Your team
settingsMembers.body: Everyone here sees the same issues, PRs and settings. The icons show which accounts each person has connected.

done.title: You're all set
done.body: Jeanclode now works in the background. You can come back to this guide anytime: click Guide in the sidebar.
